### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or public-surface change the diff implies, named right or wrong.

1. **`{ emailField }` is delivered as the spec declares it — RIGHT, with one declaration still contradicting it.** The runtime treats the form only as the whole `recipients` value (`isEmailFieldRecipient(cfg.recipients)` after `parseNodeConfig` with `NotifyConfigSchema`; a list entry never parses), and the same parse enforces `channels: 'email'` alone at run time (the spec's superRefine runs inside `parseNodeConfig`, so a node naming `inbox` beside it fails before any read). Templated through the ordinary payload, mailed through the unchanged email channel (`EMAIL_SHAPE` literal branch), and logged as a `sys_notification` event plus a `sys_notification_delivery` row (pinned, A). The field's `email` type is judged by lint at publish, as the spec's section note says; the runtime does not re-check the type and instead requires one address — consistent with the declaration. Ruling 6377887204's four conditions (email-typed record field only; templated; rate-limited per address; logged) are each met. ⚠ The spec `describe` still says "Delivery to an email-field recipient is not live yet … a run that reaches the node fails there" — false once this merges; see ③ F4.

The counter resolves the kernel `cache` at count time (the reference pattern AGENTS.md names). A counter `get`/`set` fault admits with one `warn` per process (`counterFaultWarned` is never reset) — the SMS quota's precedent; neither the changeset nor flows.mdx says the limit is best-effort. Flag, ③ F3.

3. **The computed-address screen — WRONG: it is bypassed by the one spelling the chain mails without any directory lookup.** `readsAsAddress` returns `false` for any value with a `user:` / `role:` / `team:` / `owner_of:` prefix, so such a value is never put in `computed` and goes to messaging unscreened. Read in the cited code: the resolver's `resolveOne` strips `user:` and returns the remainder as the recipient id with NO `sys_user` lookup (`recipient-resolver.ts`, `if (value.startsWith('user:')) return [value.slice(5)]`); the outbox row's `recipientId` is that remainder; the email channel's `resolveRecipient` then takes `EMAIL_SHAPE(recipient)` as a literal address and sends to it (`email-channel.ts`, the branch E3 relies on for the written-out constant). So in a node whose `channels` include `email`, an envelope over record text that evaluates to `user:stranger@outside.example` — six characters a visitor can type into the same text field — mails `stranger@outside.example`, a user holds it or not. That is the path ruling 6386629237 B closes (「若由表达式（CEL 信封）求值得到一个不属于任何用户的邮箱地址，节点失败」, read with 6377887204's 「⛔ 不接受自由文本或表达式拼出的地址（否则就是一个对外群发口）」) and the one the PR's own docblock says is closed ("an address built from record text lets whoever typed that text choose who this flow mails"). The mirror in `readsAsAddress` reproduces the resolver's `looksLikeEmail`, but the chain reads an address in TWO places, and the second (the email channel on the resolved id) is the one the `user:` prefix reaches. `owner_of:OBJ:ID` is the same class one step removed (it mails the owner field's stored value when that value is address-shaped, which app-showcase's `owner` is), but the address there comes from a stored field, not from the visitor's text; `role:` and `team:` yield `user_id` columns and are clean. No pin covers the `user:` spelling (E1–E6 test bare addresses only). Finding F1, FAIL-grade: the narrowing as declared ("a recipient that a value expression evaluates to and that reads as an email address … fails the node when no user holds it") is not what the runtime enforces on the mail path.

4. **The screen's scope and the two sides it keeps — RIGHT where it applies.** A computed address a user holds resolves to that user's id (E2); a written-out string never enters `computed` and is sent as written (E3) — ruling B's 「元数据里写死的地址是作者常量，照常发出」; no data engine or a failing lookup fails the node (E4) rather than sending unchecked — stricter than the ruling's letter in the direction the ruling points, and declared in the changeset. The channel gate (`toStringList(cfg.channels).includes('email')`) is sound on the pushed scope: `['inbox']` is the messaging default (`requestedChannels = input.channels?.length ? input.channels : ['inbox']`), and the email channel is the only one that treats an address-shaped recipient id as a destination (the SMS channel's literal branch is `PHONE_SHAPE`). See ③ F2 for the open confirmation.

5. **`isOneAddress` refuses values the `email` field type admits — a refusal the declarations do not say.** The intent is ruled (6377887204, 「访客输入同样净化」), and the list/separator/display-name/header-break/`role:` cases are right and pinned (B). But the grammar is ASCII-only (`^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$` per domain label; the RFC 5322 atext class per local-part atom), so an internationalised address — a non-ASCII domain label or local part, a quoted local part, an IP-literal domain — that the `email` validator stored is refused with "does not hold one email address", which is false for it. flows.mdx and the changeset say "exactly one mailbox, `name@example.com`: no list, display name or separator" and nowhere "ASCII only". Flag F5: state the restriction where the author reads it, or admit non-ASCII labels; a wrong refusal message is the smaller half.

6. **Public surface — RIGHT, `Clause-②: no` holds.** The two new `export const`s (`EMAIL_FIELD_SENDS_PER_WINDOW`, `EMAIL_FIELD_SEND_WINDOW_SECONDS`) are module exports only: `builtin/index.ts` re-exports `registerNotifyNode` by name and nothing else, so the package's published surface does not widen. The changeset's "exported constants, one place to change" reads as if a consumer could import them; a nit, not a finding. The spec's accepted shape is untouched (`packages/spec/**` not in the diff, as claimed).

7. **Dependency move — accepted, mis-described.** `@objectstack/plugin-auth` dev → runtime dependency of `@objectstack/service-automation` IS a new workspace edge (service-automation → plugin-auth → better-auth, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/service-messaging`); "no new graph edge" is true only of the hoisted runtime/cli closure. - **F2 — open question 1 (channel scope of ruling B), put to the maintainer as a confirmation.** The head is sound on its pushed scope (①.4): only the email channel delivers to the raw address; inbox-only nodes mail nobody; app-showcase's inbox-only owner envelopes keep working, which keeps the ruling's 「B 不拒绝任何现有配置」 true.
